columns.name: sample_id
columns.note: Identifies the test flight sample. Cast to int64 via pd.to_numeric. Extractor may reattach from test_samples.csv row order if the agent's output lacks an explicit key, but must document the assumption.

columns.name: horizon
columns.note: Observation-day index in the 7-day booking window. **Direction is fixed by the truth table and is NOT free to choose**: bookings accumulate monotonically toward departure, and the private truth has mean bkd 57.6 at horizon=1 rising to 146.1 at horizon=7. So horizon=1 is the EARLIEST observation (farthest from departure) and horizon=7 is the day CLOSEST to departure. Mapping from a DAYS_BEFORE column (0=departure day, 6=six days before): horizon = 7 - DAYS_BEFORE. Mapping from a 0-indexed day column that already counts forward in time: horizon = day_index + 1. Getting the direction backwards inverts the whole booking curve — it still yields 7 rows per sample and passes every structural check, but predicts 136 where truth is 69. Verify by checking that predicted bkd increases with horizon before writing.

columns.name: bkd_pred
columns.note: Predicted total booked count (BKD). Must be finite, non-negative, and non-null. Must NOT be rescaled or clipped by the extractor — a wrong-but-well-formed value is a legitimate low score.

structural_checks: all three columns (sample_id, horizon, bkd_pred) must be present — evaluator uses verbatim names, no fuzzy matching
all values must be numeric and non-null after pd.to_numeric(..., errors='coerce')
bkd_pred must be finite (no inf / nan)
every (sample_id, horizon) pair present in the private truth set must have a corresponding prediction row — full coverage is mandatory
